symbols.name: half root of unity
symbols.meaning: A complex number whose square is ω.
symbols.quote: Let $w = e^{\pi i/q}$ be the number whose square is $\omega$, so that $w^2 = \omega$.

symbols.name: reduced index
symbols.meaning: The reduced index (k-j) mod q, an integer from 0 to q-1.
symbols.quote: Define $b_\ell = w^{-\ell^2}$ for $\ell \in \{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, where $\ell$ is the reduced index $(k-j) \bmod q$, an integer from 0 to $q-1$.

symbols.name: index shift
symbols.meaning: An arbitrary integer shift of the index, used to show the chirp is periodic in q.
symbols.quote: For any integer $p$, $w^{-(p+q)^2} = w^{-p^2}$, because $w^{-2pq} = \omega^{-pq} = 1$ and $w^{-q^2} = (-1)^q = 1$.

relations.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) so that the transform can be computed with convolution, which the multiplication reduction needs.
It computes its transforms by a [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) multiplied by chirp factors.
